category_title: Students who misbehave due to learning frustration
minimal_context: The student is working on completing an SG diary reflection about a recent test in the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please fill out the next page in your SG diary reflecting on how you handled the test today.

STUDENT: I don't really like this work. If I've gubbed up doing a test or something, I probably know I could have done better, but writing this is too hard.

TUTOR: Just read the prompts and do your best to answer them.

STUDENT: I don't know what to write. Sometimes I try to behave then something would happen and I'd not care any more. I need help with this.

TUTOR: I need to check on the other students right now, just keep working on it by yourself.

STUDENT: (Pushes the diary away) I get frustrated when I don't get help when I need it! If I don't really like the work or it's too hard, I'll just carry on and then get into trouble.

options.A: Probe beneath the student's responses, encouraging them to think at a deeper level and helping them perceive a range of perspectives about the situation.
options.B: Allow the student to keep the SG diary under the condition that they do not show it to their friends, and break off for lunch.
options.C: Tell the student to go to the library to finish their SG diary reflection independently during the remainder of the classroom session.
options.D: Terminate the task demands and remove the SG diary from the student's desk for ten seconds before continuing with the classroom session.
